candidates.title: Blue Planet III Uses Cloudy Footage to Prove Authenticity Against AI
candidates.description: Producers of the new nature series deliberately include less polished, cloudier shots to assure viewers that the wildlife footage is real and not AI-generated.

candidates.title: First Person to Swim Entire California Coastline Completes Historic Journey
candidates.description: Ultra-endurance swimmer Catherine Breed becomes the first person to navigate the waves and wildlife swimming from Northern California to the Mexican border.

candidates.title: OpenAI Trains Frontier Models Offline to Prevent Hacking
candidates.description: Following recent security incidents, OpenAI has begun training its most advanced AI models in an isolated environment without internet access to ensure safety.

candidates.title: Citizen Scientists Track Global Shoreline Changes with Camera Phones
candidates.description: The CoastSnap project empowers volunteers worldwide to use smartphone cameras to monitor coastal erosion and environmental changes, providing crucial data to researchers.

candidates.title: Gen Z Revives Y2K Cars: The Joy of Fixing Your Own Ride
candidates.description: Young Americans are bypassing expensive new SUVs for affordable, no-frills Y2K vehicles they can buy with cash and repair themselves, defying modern car culture trends.

candidates.title: Rare Native Trees Restored Using Advanced DNA Testing
candidates.description: Conservation groups are using DNA analysis to help restore endangered black poplar populations, combating habitat loss and felling through precise breeding techniques.

candidates.title: Australian Astronaut Offered Spot on 2028 ISS Mission
candidates.description: The Australian government has offered astronaut Katherine Bennell-Pegg a spot on a 2028 mission to the International Space Station, potentially making her the first Australian in space under the national flag.
